Hi Edy,

I see what you mean now, thank you for clarifying. This problem exists in standard factor analysis as well, and has to do with the rotational/estimation indeterminacy problem. Basically the idea is this, if you estimated your unidimensional model with all negative starting value slopes, the solution would converge to the same values. However, the slopes would have their signs completely flipped because. 

So if you had the slopes a1 = (1.5, 0.5, 0.6, 1.2, ....) this would fit exactly as well as a1 = (-1.5, -0.5, -0.6, -1.2, ....). What you've noticed is that after rotation the signs of one of the factor will mainly be negatives, giving the opposite pattern of factor scores you wanted. It's not an issue, since you always can switch the signs manually if you see that in summary(mod) there are too many negatives in the loadings for your liking.

That being said, I must have changed something on the dev version since the first factor seems to be mostly positive for these data, so the issue doesn't seem to arise. Nevertheless, it's always possible to have this happen during estimation and rotation, so it's good to know about. Here's what I get on the latest dev version, and you'll probably notice the signs are different in your summary() statement.

Phil

Hi Edy, 

Part of the reason is some of the package internals in the M-step have changed to help in approximating the S-EM based information matrix. To get more consistent estimates, pass a smaller tolerance criteria such as TOL = 1e-5. The important thing to look for is that the log-likelihood doesn't change any more regardless of how small the TOL value is, and this location should be consistent across versions. Cheers.

Phil

Em quinta-feira, 23 de janeiro de 2014 22h51min50s UTC-2, Phil Chalmers escreveu:
Hi Edy,

I see what you mean now, thank you for clarifying. This problem exists in standard factor analysis as well, and has to do with the rotational/estimation indeterminacy problem. Basically the idea is this, if you estimated your unidimensional model with all negative starting value slopes, the solution would converge to the same values. However, the slopes would have their signs completely flipped because. 

So if you had the slopes a1 = (1.5, 0.5, 0.6, 1.2, ....) this would fit exactly as well as a1 = (-1.5, -0.5, -0.6, -1.2, ....). What you've noticed is that after rotation the signs of one of the factor will mainly be negatives, giving the opposite pattern of factor scores you wanted. It's not an issue, since you always can switch the signs manually if you see that in summary(mod) there are too many negatives in the loadings for your liking.

That being said, I must have changed something on the dev version since the first factor seems to be mostly positive for these data, so the issue doesn't seem to arise. Nevertheless, it's always possible to have this happen during estimation and rotation, so it's good to know about. Here's what I get on the latest dev version, and you'll probably notice the signs are different in your summary() statement.

Phil
